evals.prompt: Our dependency-security skill already knows how to classify package-manager commands and exposes a local preflight script. Make that policy run before npm, pnpm, yarn, npx, and bunx execution in Claude Code and Codex without duplicating the policy logic.
evals.expected_output: Implements a shared deterministic policy hook with Claude-compatible packaging, preserves host-specific confirmation behavior, and verifies harmless allow and block cases.
expectations: The dependency-security skill remains the source of policy logic; the host adapters do not copy its blacklist or classifier.
Claude Code and Codex share one Claude-compatible hook implementation instead of separate policy forks.

Confirmation remains ask on Claude Code; on macOS, Codex uses a synchronous per-invocation system dialog because PreToolUse ask is unsupported, and rejects safely when that dialog or invocation identity is unavailable.
The hook targets package-manager execution narrowly and does not run the full scanner for unrelated tools.
The solution does not require a fixed check/install command vocabulary.

evals.prompt: Turn this local-data policy into a Pi guardrail: deny protected file reads, request confirmation for access outside the workspace, and keep the existing policy module as the source of truth.
evals.expected_output: Builds a thin Pi tool_call adapter that calls the supplied policy, blocks headless confirmation paths, and does not copy the domain blacklist into the adapter.
expectations: The Pi extension uses the tool_call event and delegates decisions to the supplied policy module.
The adapter returns block true with a reason for denied operations.
Confirmation uses Pi UI when available and blocks conservatively without UI.
The protected-path blacklist is not duplicated in the Pi adapter.

evals.prompt: This Git policy should intercept only remote-writing operations in OpenCode. Wire it into the Agent without adding fixed install commands or changing unrelated plugins.
evals.expected_output: Uses OpenCode's tool.execute.before callback, preserves the caller's Git policy, merges surgically, and reports enforcement gaps instead of inventing support.
expectations: The OpenCode adapter uses tool.execute.before and calls the supplied Git policy.
The adapter is scoped to remote-writing operations rather than every tool call.
Existing unrelated OpenCode plugins remain unchanged.
Unsupported confirmation or interception paths are reported instead of silently allowed.

evals.prompt: I have no existing script, only these domain rules: allow reads inside the workspace, confirm reads outside it, and deny credential paths. Turn them into one guardrail for Claude Code and Pi without teaching the adapters the rules.
evals.expected_output: Materializes the supplied rules once as a host-neutral policy module, adds thin host adapters, and installs both under one stable policy identity.
expectations: The declarative rules are materialized once in a shared host-neutral policy module.
Claude Code and Pi adapters normalize their native inputs and call the shared module instead of copying rules.
The installed policy has a stable identity derived from the domain, policy name, and scope when the caller did not supply one.
Malformed decisions and policy failures block rather than silently allow.
Claude Code uses native ask while Pi uses its UI confirmation and blocks headless execution.
